key_insight: SpaceNum shows that numeric outputs from Vision–Language Models are not reliably grounded in spatial perception: many VLMs produce plausible-looking numbers (e.g., distances, coordinates, magnitudes) without true spatial understanding. By evaluating numbers as both dynamic transitions and static coordinates, SpaceNum exposes systematic gaps in spatial numerical grounding.
problem_solved: Clarifies whether and how VLM-generated numbers (action magnitudes, spatial coordinates) reflect genuine spatial perception rather than learned token patterns, providing a unified benchmark to evaluate spatial numerical grounding in embodied and vision-language settings.
method: Define two complementary task families: numbers-as-dynamic-transitions (e.g., action magnitudes, step-wise displacements) and numbers-as-static-coordinates (e.g., absolute/relative positions).
Construct a controllable dataset and evaluation protocol (synthetic + real images, paired ground-truth numeric labels) to probe numeric grounding across scales and contexts.
Apply standardized metrics and systematic ablations to evaluate popular VLMs, isolating failure modes (scale sensitivity, context leaks, token bias) and comparing model behaviors.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical benchmark to diagnose and improve numeric/spatial reliability in VLMs for robotics, navigation, and embodied agents; informs dataset design, model calibration, and evaluation practices to ensure numeric outputs are spatially grounded.
visual_elements: Task taxonomy diagram showing the two task families: dynamic transitions vs static coordinates with example inputs/outputs.
Bar/heatmap comparing model accuracy/error by numeric magnitude and task type (revealing scale-dependent failures).
Pair of image examples annotated with ground-truth numbers vs model predictions to illustrate correct vs spurious numeric outputs.
Calibration/error-distribution plots and a checklist infographic for practitioners (diagnostics + mitigation tips).
paper_title: SPACENUM: Revisiting Spatial Numerical Understanding in VLMs
paper_authors: Jianshu Zhang, Yijiang Li, Huifeixin Chen, Haoran Lu, Letian Xue
